messages.author: 84e6ff87e445f88b
messages.subject: lavTestWald() and anova()
parts:
Dear All,
The new lavTestWald() function in 0.5.-16 version is perfect for me as I have a series of tests involving constraints! I wonder what is the difference between that and the lavTestLRT() command between one unconstrained and one constrained model. In the syntax below I don't get the same values. And also the values change when using estimator="MLR" so that it takes into account the estimator but I'm not sure how. Could anyone explain to me 1) the difference between the two methods and 2) if one of them should be preferably chosen when testing a simple constraint like param1==param2 , with or without MLR.
Thank You!!
JB

HS.model <- '
    visual  =~ x1 + b1*x2 + x3
textual =~ x4 + b2*x5 + x6
speed   =~ x7 + b3*x8 + x9
'
HS.model1 <- '
    visual  =~ x1 + b1*x2 + x3
textual =~ x4 + b2*x5 + x6
speed   =~ x7 + b3*x8 + x9
b1==0
'

fit <- cfa(HS.model, data=HolzingerSwineford1939)
fit1 <- cfa(HS.model1, data=HolzingerSwineford1939)

lavTestLRT(fit,fit1)
lavTestWald(fit, constraints = "b1 == 0")

fit <- cfa(HS.model, data=HolzingerSwineford1939,estimator="MLR")
fit1 <- cfa(HS.model1, data=HolzingerSwineford1939,estimator="MLR")

lavTestLRT(fit,fit1)
lavTestWald(fit, constraints = "b1 == 0")

parts:
On 03/11/2014 07:42 PM, JB wrote:
> anyone explain to me 1) the difference between the two methods

The difference between the Wald test and the LR test can be found in
many textbooks. A classic reference is

Buse, A. (1982). The likelihood ratio, Wald, and Langrange Multiplier
Tests: An Expository Note. The American Statistician, 36(3), 153-157.

A google search revealed this link:

http://www.uh.edu/~cmurray/courses/econ_7331/Trilogy%20of%20Tests.pdf

2) if
> one of them should be preferably chosen when testing a simple constraint
> like param1==param2 , with or without MLR.

That, I do not know. I would think the reasoning does not change if we
go from ML to MLR, but I have no reference to back this up.

Yves.
